title: Fieldwatch pocket notes — 2028-02-14
content:
Fieldwatch shift notes (short-form)
Date: 2028-02-14
Owner: Evan Mercer (oncall)

---
Key context (quick):
- Early morning noise: elevated 503 rate from hosted-ingest gateway (spike ~03:12–03:26 UTC).
- Primary user impact: short-lived latency for model upload endpoints; client retries masked some errors.
- Escalation: routed to infra -> autoscaler -> serving-runtime.

Timeline (handy timestamps):
- 03:09: alert fired: gated-503s > 0.5% (5m)
- 03:12: spike peaks, concurrent 12 small jobs stuck in queue on pool-a
- 03:15: I paged infra oncall (Harold) — he confirmed autoscaler throttle + race in drain hook
- 03:20: temporarily increased pool-a max nodes to +2 (manual scale) — immediate drop in queue
- 03:26: error rate dropped, alert closed 03:36 as steady state recovered
- 04:00: follow-up note posted in JIRA INFR-3421 

Immediate actions taken (commands & links):
- checked queues: /usr/local/bin/rwctl queue status --pool pool-a --json
- scaled: rwctl cluster scale pool-a --add 2 --reason "temp oncall manual bump" (command run from bastion-ops)
- log tail: sudo journalctl -u rw-serving -f --since "2028-02-14 03:00" | grep "enqueue" | grep "pool-a" > /tmp/pool-a-enqueue.txt
- linked trace sample: https://observability.redwood.example/traces/trace-8b3f6a (copied to JIRA)

Runbook TODOs and gaps discovered (to fix later):
- RB-1: drain hook race: runbook currently tells operator to restart node, but does not mention checking long-lived job counts before restart. Add step to check "rwctl job list --state running --pool $NODE_POOL" and wait/evict gracefully.
- RB-2: add explicit instruction for manual scaling for pool-a in case autoscaler is misconfigured (thresholds and cooldowns).
- RB-3: add snippet to runbook for snapshotting kv-cache for serving-runtime before node drains (we didn't have this and cache warm-up cost was visible).
- RB-4: add alert escalation matrix: who to page at 00:00--08:00 UTC vs 08:00--24:00; current oncall rotation ambiguous.

Follow-ups created (tickets / owners):
- INFR-3421 (priority: P2) — "Investigate drain hook race & autoscaler cooldown" — assigned to Harold Chen — due 2028-02-21
- RWOPS-1280 (task) — "Add manual scaling snippet + playbook to fieldwatch runbook" — assigned to me (Evan) — WIP
- SERV-765 (investigation) — "KV-cache snapshot option for graceful drains" — triaged to runtime team (Maya)

Quick notes to self (fragments):
- check node image version on pool-a (suspect older kernel + docker runtime mismatch)
- follow up with build team on new drain-hook PR (GH: redwood/serving-runtime#1458)
- verify autoscaler cooldown values: currently 600s? confirm in RW cluster config (k8s autoscaler + local policy conf)
- ask infra to add a temporary synthetic test that simulates many small jobs arriving concurrently (to reproduce)

Paging & comms (what I said in Slack):
- to #ops-pager: "03:15 — paging infra oncall, manual +2 nodes to pool-a; collecting logs; filing INFR-3421 for follow-up"
- to #eng-runtime: "03:22 — saw enqueue backlog tied to long-running finisher task; possible drain-hook race; tag Harold and Maya"

What worked well / lessons: 
- Manual scale was quick and effective — need to keep that in the runbook as an explicit short-term mitigation.
- Observability traces made root cause candidate obvious (blocking drains) — ensure we keep that trace retention for at least 7 days for ondemand incident RCA.

Runbook TODO checklist (short):
- [ ] Insert manual scale command + explanation (RWOPS-1280)
- [ ] Add job-check before restart (RB-1)
- [ ] Add kv-cache snapshot step (RB-3)
- [ ] Clarify escalation matrix (RB-4)
- [ ] Add reproducibility test (infra)

Post-incident notes (micro-RCA draft):
- probable root cause: race in node drain hook combined with an autoscaler cooldown that prevented additional nodes from provisioning quickly enough under a burst of small jobs. The drain hook blocked eviction of several long-running finisher tasks, which caused enqueues to build up in pool-a. Manual scaling bypassed the cooldown and alleviated the queue.
- mitigation: short-term manual scale; medium-term fix: update drain hook + autoscaler config + add kv-cache snapshot.

Open questions / next sync agenda: 
- do we have any older node images still running in pool-a? how to perform a rolling image rotation without user-visible latency?
- should autoscaler be allowed a faster emergency path (manual override API for oncall) or do we add explicit runbook steps only?
- what metrics should we add to detect an impending drain-hook stall earlier? (e.g., eviction-wait-time, long-running-finisher-count)

Misc scratch leftovers (todo):
- ping Mandi to request 7-day trace retention for critical endpoints (ticket to observability team)
- follow up with Maya on SERV-765 for ETA
- draft small one-pager explaining temporary mitigation for customer-success (they asked for incident summary)

Rotation notes: 
- next oncall: Leila Ortiz (2028-02-16 00:00 UTC) — leave short handwritten notes on Slack channel and link INFR-3421

---
End of pocket notes.

(Notes are intentionally terse — will expand to incident report if pi/exec asks.)
